title: Magnetic-, Acoustic-, and Optical-Triple-Responsive Microbubbles for Magnetic Hyperthermia and Pothotothermal Combination Cancer Therapy
protocol: Disperse magnetic nanoparticles (Fe3O4, iron oxide) in deionized water to form a 10 mg/mL stock solution.
Place the tube containing the IONPs solution in an ultrasonic cleaning machine for 20 min.
Add 150 μL of deionized water, 150 μL of 10 mM sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), and 400 μL of a stock solution of IONPs to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Fix the homogenizer with a scaffold in an ice bath.
Place the tube of the mixture in an ice bath.
Adjust the homogenizer speed to 20,000 rpm and turn on the homogenizer for 3 min.
Turn off the homogenizer and remove the tube from the ice bath.
Place the tube to the tube rack for 12 h stabilization at room temperature.
Adsorb the resulted NSMs to the tube wall by a magnet and remove the supernatant.
Replenish with 1 mL of fresh deionized water.
Repeat the wash process for three times.
Resuspend NSMs in 1 mL of fresh distilled water.
Transfer 10 μL of NSMs suspension to a clean glass slide after slightly shaking.
Use a fluorescence microscope at 20x magnification to visualize NSMs morphology.
Take photos of random areas.
Measure the diameter of the NSMs from the photos using Nano Measurer 1.2 software.
Count at least 200 microbubbles.
Click “File” and then “Open” to select an image file.
Import the image.
Press the “ruler” button.
Draw a red line with the same length as the ruler.
Press “Settings” | “Ruler” and enter the length of the ruler.
Draw lines equal in length to the diameters of individual microbubbles in the image.
Complete all measurements.
Click on “Report” | “View Report”.
Dilute 200 μL of NSMs with 800 μL deionized water to form a stock solution.
Connect the function generator, amplifier, impedance matching, and homemade focused transducer.
Place the transducer in the center at the bottom of an artificial cuboid sink.
Connect the hydrophone to an oscilloscope to monitor output ultrasound intensity.
Add deionized water into the sink to immerse the transducer.
Adjust the function generator to sweep mode.
Tune the frequency range from 10 kHz to 900 kHz.
Set the amplitude to 20 Vpp (Voltage peak-peak).
Adjust the power of ultrasound to 0.1% by the amplifier.
Run each cycle for a duration of 4 seconds with an interval of 1 second between cycles.
Prepare 1 mL NSMs stock solution samples in the tube.
Fix the tube with a scaffold on top of the homemade focused transducer.
Attach the magnet to the bottom of the tube and attract the NSMs.
Turn on the power of the function generator and the amplifier.
Switch off the function generator after application of 5 cycles (25 s) of ultrasound.
Remove the magnet and collect 1 mL of the solution containing the released IONPs.
Add 1 mL of deionized water to the centrifuge tube.
Repeat step until NSMs in the tube collapse completely.
Quantify all the released IONPs by the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES).
Turn on the power supply of the laser and allow it to warm for several minutes.
Fix a fiber coupled 808 nm laser diode on a retort stand.
Direct the laser beam through an optical fiber and focus on the sample stage to achieve a 6 mm light spot by a convex lens.
Measure the power output with a laser power meter and adjust the power to 1 W/cm2.
Fix the infrared thermal imaging camera on the tripod.
Turn on the camera and check if working.
Turn off the power supply and the infrared thermal imaging camera.
Prepare a 1 mL sample at different IONPs concentrations (1.05 mg/mL, 1.35 mg/mL, 3.65 mg/mL, 5 mg/mL) in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Place the tube of interest at the focused region of the laser beam and record the baseline temperature of the sample.
Turn on the laser power and the infrared thermal imaging camera and irradiate the sample for 10 min continuously.
Record the temperature in real time during irradiation.
Turn off the laser power and infrared thermal imaging camera after 10 min of irradiation.
Wait for the temperature of the region to return to the baseline before repeating the measurement.
Use deionized water at 20 °C as a control for photothermal measurement.
Feed murine breast cancer cells (4T1) with RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin.
Set the culturing environment to 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Culture 4T1 cells in T25 flasks and passage the cells in a 1:2 ratio when 90% confluence is reached.
Rinse the cell layer with 1x PBS solution to remove residual serum containing trypsin inhibitor.
Add 2 mL of Trypsin-EDTA solution to the flask for detachment.
Add 3 mL of 1640 medium and aspirate cells by gently pipetting.
Collect 5 mL of the cell suspension and centrifuge at 500 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant and add 1 mL of fresh 1640 medium to form a cell suspension.
Add 100 μL of the cell suspension to a confocal dish containing 1 mL of the culture medium.
Place the inoculated cell culture confocal dish in an incubator for 24 h.
Dilute different concentrations (1.05 mg/mL, 1.35 mg/mL, 3.65 mg/mL, 5 mg/mL) of IONPs sample to make 1 mL solution with serum-free 1640 medium.
Aspirate the culture medium from the confocal dish and add the prepared sample solution.
Turn on the laser power and focus the laser beam at the center of the dish.
Adjust the output power to 1 W/cm².
Turn on the infrared thermal imaging camera, irradiate the cells in the confocal dish for 10 min continuously.
Record the temperature in real time for the focused region.
Turn off the laser and infrared thermal imaging camera.
Transfer the irradiated dish to the incubator for another 24 h.
Remove and discard the culture medium.
Add 1 mL of fresh culture medium in the confocal dish.
Add 5 μL of Calcein-AM solution (1 mg/mL) into the dish.
Incubate the confocal dish at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 15 min.
Rinse the cell layer with 1x PBS solution twice.
Observe and image the cells by a confocal fluorescence microscope using an excitation wavelength of 488 nm and an emission wavelength of 500-540 nm.
Choose 5 areas in the confocal images randomly.
Count the number of live 4T1 cells in each area manually.
Quantify the viability of 4T1 cells by comparing the number of live cells in all experimental groups with the control group.
Prepare 3 eight-week-old ICR male mice with a mean weight of 25 ± 2 g.
Add 2 g of gelatin powder to 20 mL of deionized water.
Heat the solution to 40 - 50 °C until the gelatin dissolves completely, forming a transparent and clear solution.
Add 100 mg IONPs to the solution from step 3.4.2.
Heat the gel to 40 – 50 °C.
Inject 500 μL of the gelatin solution into the right breast pad of the mouse immediately after mixing.
Turn on the laser power and focus the laser beam at the interest region (right breast pad).
Adjust the output power to 1 W/cm2.
Turn on the infrared thermal imaging camera.
Irradiate the interest region for 10 min continuously.
Record the temperature of the region of interest in real time.
Turn off the laser and infrared thermal imaging camera.
Turn on the chiller for 10 min and then power on the moderate radio frequency heating machine (i.e., AFM generator).
Set the parameters of the machine as follows: frequency (f) = 415 kHz, magnetic field intensity = 1.8 kA/m.
Prepare 1 mL of the sample at different IONPs concentration in a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Place the tube in the center of a water-cooled magnetic induction copper coil.
Turn on the alternating magnetic field (AFM) and the infrared thermal imaging camera.
Induce the sample for 10 min continuously and record the temperature in real time.
Wait for the temperature of the copper coil to come back to the baseline for 10 min.
Repeat the measurement of other samples following the same procedure.
Power off the moderate radio frequency heating machine (AFM).
Power off the chiller.
Prepare 3 eight-week-old ICR male mice with a mean weight of 25 ± 2 g.
Prepare 20 mL of 10% gelatin gel containing 5 mg/mL IONPs solution.
Heat the gelatin gel to 40 - 50 °C.
Inject 500 μL of the heated gelatin solution into the right breast pad of each mouse.
Turn on the alternating magnetic field (AFM).
Turn on the infrared thermal imaging camera.
Place the right breast pad of the mice in the center of a water-cooled magnetic induction copper coil.
Image the interest region (right breast pad) for 10 minutes continuously.
Record the temperature of the interest region in real time.
Turn off the power switch of the machine and infrared thermal imaging camera after 10 minutes of induction.
Wait for the temperature of the copper coil to return to baseline for 10 minutes.
Euthanize mice by CO2 asphyxiation and cervical vertebra dislocation or any method approved by the Institute’s animal research committee.
